title: Define minimal runtime assurances and acceptance flow for unpinned open-weights with soft-fallback routing
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: We continue to see requests to accept experimental open-weights (community variants) into the catalog without strict version pinning. This ticket defines the minimum runtime guarantees, acceptance signals, and an operational rollback/soft-fallback plan so catalog entries that are unpinned can be safely served in hosted and Dedicated contexts. The goal is to enable faster intake for exploratory models while protecting latency SLOs and customer-facing stability. This PRD clarifies scope, defines telemetry gates, and specifies the soft-fallback routing behavior for unpinned variants.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Catalog entry template includes a compatibility signal block with: model-arch, expected max-context, quantization-tested flags (8-bit, 4-bit), and KV-cache compatibility: true|false.
A2: Runtime must expose a per-variant p95 tail-latency metric for 256 token generations and a per-variant tokens/s throughput baseline within first 72 hours of traffic.

A3: Onboarding pipeline succeeds only if automated sanity suite (synthetic prompts + core eval set) passes: no more than 6% regression in avg response correctness vs a pinned baseline and no OOMs during 1 hour of profile runs for representative batch sizes.

A4: Soft-fallback routing policy implemented: when p95 latency breach (>2x baseline) OR error rate >1% over 10m, traffic shifts incrementally to a pinned-compatible variant or next best compatible model per routing policy; rollback runbook created.
A5: Acceptance requires documented fallback candidate(s) in the model catalog entry and an owner declared (team/individual) for emergency rollbacks.
A6: Security & provenance checks completed: license compatibility verified, weights provenance field populated, and security_review_required flag set if the model is from an unverified source.
A7: Dashboard tile and alert runbook created for each unpinned intake with links to: profiling logs, example failing traces, and the GitHub PR with onboarding artifacts.
A8: If a model is marked 'no-KV-cache', runtime prevents KV cache usage and the intake must include a compatibility note explaining functional implications; acceptance blocked without this note.
scope_changes: Originally: allow ad-hoc unpinned variants in catalog with minimal metadata. Now: require a lightweight runtime compatibility declaration and profiling artifact before entry moves to 'Available' state.
Introduce a mandatory 72-hour profiling window post-ingress for unpinned variants before they can receive >5% of real traffic.
Add new telemetry keys (catalog.variant.p95_256, catalog.variant.err_rate_10m, catalog.variant.kv_support) to standard ingestion schema.
decisions: Decision 1: Accept unpinned variants only behind a soft-fallback routing policy; disallow direct primary route without fallback candidate.
Decision 2: Require a minimal automated sanity-suite (open-source core eval set) for any variant that will serve production traffic within 72 hours of ingestion.
Decision 3: For Dedicated customers, catalog entry will indicate if variant is 'supported' or 'experimental'. Dedicated instances may opt-out of experimental variants via config.
tradeoffs: Faster intake vs. increased operational risk: requiring profiling delays availability but reduces regressions and incidents.
Block on KV-cache compatibility reduces feature mismatch but may exclude some models; we allow a 'no-KV-cache' path with explicit warning and lower allowed traffic caps.
More telemetry increases storage/alerting costs; we will roll out telemetry keys incrementally and cap retention for experimental variants.
dependencies: ENG-50214 (runtime: per-variant telemetry and routing API)
DES-2112 (catalog UI: intake form additions for compatibility declarations)
PM-905467 (related: onboarding PRD for beta open models)
